messages.text:
Hi Mike,
 
I hope you’re doing well.
 
I’m writing regarding our scheduled customer interview on October 16, 2026, at
10:30 PM (Italian time).
 
I joined the Google Meet link at the scheduled time and waited to be admitted to
the meeting. Unfortunately, nobody admitted me, and after waiting, the
connection eventually timed out.
 
The same situation occurred yesterday, when I also attempted to join at the
agreed time but was unable to speak with you.
 
I genuinely appreciated your invitation and made myself available for both
appointments, setting aside my personal time to participate and share my
experience as a HeliumDeploy customer.
 
Unfortunately, despite my willingness to participate, neither interview could
take place.
 
Considering that I made two genuine attempts to attend the scheduled meetings, I
would kindly ask whether you could still honor the $50 thank-you compensation
mentioned in your original invitation, as the interviews could not be completed
due to circumstances beyond my control.
 
I have screenshots documenting my attempt to join the meeting and would be happy
to provide them if needed.
 
Thank you for your understanding. I look forward to hearing from you.
 
Best regards,
Francesco C.
 
Il 13/10/2026 19:25 CEST Mike T. <(email hidden)
[(email hidden)]> ha scritto:
 
 
Hi Francesco,
 
Mike here, from HeliumDeploy.
 
You ordered from us recently, and I am running customer interviews
with people who did. Mostly I want to know how you found us and why
you picked us over everywhere else you could have gone.
 
If you are waiting on a batch unit, I can give you the latest on yours
while we are on.
 
Fifteen minutes, video or phone. There is a $50 thank you at the end of it.
 
https://calendly.com/mike-heliumdeploy/30min
[https://calendly.com/mike-heliumdeploy/30min]
 
If none of the slots work, just reply to this one and we will sort
something out.
 
Thanks either way,
Mike
Handed to the team · Interview compensation promised by Mike; only a person can honour or rebook it.

Hi Francesco,

Thank you for writing, and I'm sorry you sat waiting twice for a call that never opened. That's on us, not on you, and I understand the frustration of setting aside your evening two nights running for nothing.

I've passed this straight to Mike and the team with the detail you gave, including both attempts. The team is offline for the evening and picks it up tomorrow from 10am Eastern, and the answer will come to you as a reply in this thread, so there is nothing you need to resend. Please hold on to the screenshots in case they ask, but you don't need to send them now.

If you'd still like to do the interview, say the word in your reply and we'll arrange a time that suits you in Italy rather than late at night.

Best regards,
Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Hi Sarah,
 
thank you for your reply and for confirming that the two missed interviews were
due to an issue on your side.
 
I would still be happy to participate in the interview at a time that is
convenient in Italy.
 
However, I would also like to clarify the point I raised in my previous email
regarding the $50 thank-you compensation.
 
Since I joined both scheduled meetings on time, waited to be admitted, and set
aside my personal time on two separate evenings, I would kindly ask whether
HeliumDeploy can still honor the $50 compensation for those two unsuccessful
interview attempts, regardless of whether we subsequently reschedule the
interview.
 
I am of course happy to provide the screenshots showing both attempts if needed.
 
Please let me know what the team decides on this point, and I would also be
happy to arrange a new interview time that works better for Italy.
 
Best regards,
Francesco

Hi Francesco,

Understood, and your point is a fair one. You showed up twice at the agreed time and the fault was ours, so I've put the request for the $50 in front of Mike exactly as you've framed it, as compensation for the two attempts and separate from any rescheduled call. It isn't mine to approve, so I won't promise you an outcome I don't control, but it is with the team now and they pick it up today from 10am Eastern. Their answer comes back to you in this thread.

On the interview, I'd be glad to get it rebooked. Italy is six hours ahead of Eastern, so an afternoon slot for Mike lands early evening for you. If you reply with two or three times that suit you, in Italian time, I'll pass them on so Mike can confirm one rather than sending you back to the calendar.

No need to send the screenshots unless the team asks for them.

Best regards,
Sarah, HeliumDeploy

Hello HeliumDeploy Team,

I have already purchased a Harlo B30 miner from your store, and I am currently preparing a dedicated ventilated rack cabinet for its installation.

Before purchasing the cabinet, I would appreciate your confirmation of a few technical details.

1. Exact dimensions and weight

Could you please provide the exact external dimensions of the complete Harlo B30 (width × height × depth, in millimetres), including any protruding components?

2. Airflow direction

Could you confirm the exact airflow direction?

* Do the rear-mounted fans draw cool air into the miner and exhaust hot air through the opposite side?

* Or do they extract hot air from the heatsink toward the rear?

3. Rack installation and ventilation

I am considering a 12U or 15U rack cabinet with a depth of 450 mm, featuring a perforated front door and ventilated side panels.

Could you please clarify:

* What minimum clearance should be maintained around the air intake and exhaust?

* Can the B30 safely operate rotated 90 degrees horizontally, with its intake and exhaust facing the rack's perforated side panels?

* Would you recommend this arrangement for continuous 24/7 operation?

* Are there any specific ventilation or ambient-temperature recommendations for installing the B30 inside a rack cabinet?

My goal is to ensure proper cooling, long-term reliability and safe operation without restricting airflow.

Thank you very much for your assistance.

Best regards
